claims.statement: The scheduler graph is a single-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered as the `scheduler` assistant in langgraph.json; its `_launch` node deterministically dispatches a tick without invoking an LLM.

The scheduler routes recognized tasks for reconcile, baby-sit, expedited review, background tasks, workspace refresh (including legacy environment_refresh), session cost, thread feedback, and agent cost; only the unmatched path calls launch_scheduled_agent_run(schedule_id).
When a keyed scheduler tick lacks watch_key, thread_id, or schedule_id, `_launch` returns a `missing_*` status rather than raising.
Dashboard-managed recurring schedules validate and normalize a five-field cron expression, range-checking numbers, steps, ranges, and lists before schedule storage.

Schedule definitions and run state use separate namespaces; scheduler launch loads a schedule and only launches records whose trigger is `schedule`, while run state retains latest thread/run/trigger/error fields.

reconcile_stale_runs is the durable-dispatch safety net: it paginates every busy thread, lists pending runs, and interrupts runs older than max_age_seconds (default 1800 seconds) so a lost completion does not hold a thread busy forever.
The reconcile sweep isolates per-thread failures and returns counts of threads checked, stale runs found, and runs cancelled.

Session-cost refresh uses a self-terminating chain of stateless delayed scheduler runs: each attempt updates a correlated Slack footer or, only for a transient pending result, schedules the next attempt from a fixed five-delay list.

Each baby-sit watch is persisted in `baby_sit_watches` under a lower-cased owner/repo#pr_number key and binds the originating thread, PR head SHA/ref, installation, captured run configuration, and SourceContext along with durable retry and dedupe state.
Only one active thread can watch a PR: start_watch rejects another thread, preserves retry/dedupe state only for the same head SHA, and resets it for a new head.
start_watch idempotently ensures one per-watch LangGraph cron, reusing a matching cron and deleting duplicates; a brand-new watch is rolled back if cron creation fails.
Each baby-sit watch has a fixed UTC `*/10 * * * *` scheduler cron; evaluation returns statuses such as pending, settling, or duplicate without dispatching an agent run when CI state is unchanged.

The GitHub webhook route verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 before processing, and handle_ci_webhook ignores non-failing CI payloads, matches active watches by head SHA or branch, and de-duplicates delivery IDs.
Webhook and cron triggers funnel into evaluation under a per-watch short-lived lock thread, so one watch evaluates at a time and concurrent triggers do not dispatch duplicate failure runs.

A new head SHA resets baby-sit retry, settlement, and dispatch/alert dedupe state; a new failure fingerprint dispatches a confidence-gated `/baby-sit --continue` run to the origin thread and removes that fingerprint if dispatch fails.
Baby-sit signals success only after the exact check-set fingerprint has been stable for CHECK_SET_SETTLE_MINUTES (10 minutes), preventing premature green while checks are added.
Flaky reruns are capped at three per head SHA; record_retry enforces ownership and matching head, persists the increment, and alerts only once per head/check/safe GitHub URL.

Baby-sit stops on closed/merged PRs, settled success, blocked checks, retry exhaustion, or three evaluation errors, notifying the source context when possible and otherwise enqueuing a `/baby-sit --terminal` run before stopping the watch.

manage_baby_sit is the agent-facing durable-watch tool: it requires a canonical PR URL and executable thread, validates GitHub access/open PR/head/App installation on start, and enforces thread ownership for stop and retry recording.

Background-task monitoring is model-free: ensure_background_task_cron idempotently registers one every-minute `background_tasks` cron per thread, and monitor_background_tasks atomically claims each terminal notification, enqueues it to the origin thread, and removes monitor crons only after a locked fresh recheck finds no running or pending work.

schedule_thread_wakeup schedules a one-shot re-trigger of the current agent thread from 1 minute to 24 hours as a thread-bound cron against the `agent` assistant, with an end_time about 90 seconds past firing and selected configuration propagated to a default or supplied system prompt.

Thread wakeups are budget-limited to at most 10 between human messages, keyed to the latest human-message generation; a new human message resets the budget but a system message does not, and the budget is persisted before cron creation.
Because fired wakeup cron rows remain stored, schedule_thread_wakeup best-effort purges only expired `thread_wakeup` crons, fully paging matching rows before deletion.

The baby-sit skill directs cloud runs to the durable webhook-plus-ten-minute-fallback watch, while local/desktop runs use a bounded foreground `gh pr checks --watch` loop and do not call manage_baby_sit or schedule_thread_wakeup.

Agent-cost refresh schedules at most five stateless delayed scheduler attempts, fetches run-only LangSmith cost, persists it to the invocation usage record, and terminates on unavailable input/data or retry exhaustion.

Focused tests cover baby-sit lifecycle, concurrency and deduplication, signed CI routing, stale-run pagination and failure isolation, bounded cost refresh, and wakeup validation, correlation, limits, concurrency, and cleanup.

A feedback delayed scheduler run verifies the saved event under an agent-thread state lock, defers while the thread is busy or active, skips obsolete/non-successful work, and marks a matching feedback record ready before posting its Slack prompt.

Workspace refresh registers a deterministic per-workspace daily scheduler cron; full refresh starts from the base snapshot and runs setup plus update, whereas update starts from the ready snapshot and runs only update.

Workspace refresh prevents overlapping plausible jobs, captures a new snapshot only after all scripts succeed, stops the builder sandbox, and records failure without replacing the prior ready snapshot.
